_doc: Stream C/E (play-test 4 S4): champions and rares in the wilds. Every ordinary monster a WILDS camp spawns (not a named rare, an encounter, an escort or a dungeon body) rolls a rank: `chance.rare` then `chance.champion`, from `chance.minLevel` up. A champion carries one modifier, a rare two and a name of its own (Farhold's ranks: balance.ranks hp/dmg/armour/xp/gold and better loot — dropBonus +1/+2, dropRarity x1.5/x2.2 — plus data/enemies.json's 22 modifiers). Thousandvale adds `extra` modifiers (same fields as Farhold's: prefix, hp, dmg, armor, speed, scale, onHit, aura, fx; `escort` = how many of its own kind follow it), a size floor per rank (`size`, so a champion is visibly bigger even with no `giant` roll), and `abilities`: a telegraphed special per modifier (docs/encounters.md specials format) added to the monster's own family specials, so a Fiery wolf throws fire as well as biting. `rareNames` builds a rare's own name: '<given> the <epithet>'. Rares and champions come with an `aff` list and a `sc` (scale) on their entity info for the client.

chance._minLevel: play-test 5 T10 ('I still haven't seen one'): champion 0.09 -> 0.05 (E's 62 roadside champions are placed on top), rare 0.025 -> 0.06, and from level 2 instead of 4 — a level-1 monster never rolls (the very first fights stay plain), and a camp E marks `noRank` never rolls (measured through the real spawn path in tests/C/playtest5-loot: before 0% at levels 1-3 and 2.7% rare / 9% champion from 4; after 6% rare / 5% champion from level 2)
